clinician.final_diagnosis: Postmortem brain autopsy was positive for CJD
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man presented with sudden-onset motor, functional, and cognitive decline, initially raising suspicion for stroke. Initial CT brain was normal, ruling out acute intracranial pathology. Subsequent MRI brain revealed bilateral cortical ribboning on DWI and FLAIR, highly suggestive of sCJD. General CSF analysis showed no cells, normal glucose and protein, and no oligoclonal bands, ruling out common inflammatory/infectious causes. EEG showed diffuse encephalopathy but lacked specific CJD patterns. The diagnosis was ultimately confirmed by postmortem brain autopsy positive for CJD.
